content: The use of estrogen without a progestin can increase the risk of developing breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The likelihood of these severe side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of its use. It is recommended to use this medication at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest possible time. Regularly discuss the necessity of continuing this medication with your doctor, ideally every 3 to 6 months. If long-term use is required, you should undergo regular comprehensive physical exams, such as annually, as directed by your physician. This medication is a hormone (estrogen) used by women to alleviate symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to reduced estrogen production in the body. Certain estrogen products may also be prescribed to postmenopausal women to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis). However, alternative medications like raloxifene or bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate) may also effectively prevent bone loss and could be safer options. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. If you are prescribed extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the entire drug at once, increasing the risk of side effects. To maximize the benefits, take the medication regularly and at the same time(s) each day. Follow your dosing schedule carefully. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal complications from blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms or side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the U.S., you can also call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control assistance. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco, as these can increase the risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions also elevate the risk of blood clots. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin or face (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, potentially affecting their growth and development. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Discuss breastfeeding with your doctor before using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. While taking this medication, regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted as directed by your doctor. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help. Engage in mental exercises like reading or solving puzzles to help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercise, quit smoking, limit alcohol intake, and consume a well-balanced diet with adequate calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
